title: Palette proposal: the chart tokens for Phase 3, round 0
author: Data visualization and systems lead, with the design director's eye
status: Proposed. Every token here is marked "Proposed until board 1" in its description; Dustin approves the new colors on board 1. The engineer adds them as one pre-release under Rule 26.8.

release_suggestion.why: Rule 26.8: before 6.0.0, every change raises the number after the hyphen. The Gate 2 drafts ran gate2.1 to gate2.9; this is the first draft on the way to Gate 3. The engineer names the release

change_note.tokens: oa.color.tint.prussianN56 and prussianN29 (new); oa.chart.color.diverging on Charcoal; oa.chart.color.categorical; oa.chart.color.ghost; oa.chart.grade; the descriptions listed under description_changes
change_note.change: Two new colors, both Prussian mixed toward Newsprint, so the diverging scale works on Charcoal. New roles with no new value: the four-ink categorical set with its label inks, the ghost lines of small multiples, and the evidence line code as stroke styles. Every new token is marked proposed until board 1.
change_note.reason: Dark mode needs the diverging scale on Charcoal (DR-204); the categorical set stays with the four brand inks and no new hue (DR-234); the line code moves out of three build scripts into the tokens (Gate 1, M1; Rule 10.10).
change_note.record: DR-204, DR-234, D2-95, Gate 1 M1, Rule 10.10; the palette notes' D3 calls

not_added: A Prussian sequential scale: no chart in S01 to S16 or in rounds 1 and 2's plan as read today needs a second measure in sequence (proposal section 1.6 adds it only on need)
Chart tokens on White: a printed report prints the Newsprint values on the paper (DR-53); this sheet measures them on White and they hold
Chart tokens on Prussian: Prussian is a data ink in two palettes, and red never sits on it (Rule 05.3); a chart in a Prussian panel sits on its own Newsprint or Charcoal plate
A new red or a red tint: the red-on-red specimen resolves by Rule 05.3's order, with the point yielding to ink (Rule 11.16)

needs.N-10: Diverging pair B on Charcoal for the dark theme (DR-204): the scale has Newsprint tokens only, and the dark theme sets it to initial. Measured on this sheet
needs.N-11: A categorical set of up to four groups (DR-234): no token names the four brand inks as groups, with a label ink for each and the hatch that keeps Verdigris and Stone apart (D2-95)
needs.N-12: The evidence line code (Gate 1, M1; Rule 10.10) as tokens, so the chart kit, chapter 13 and chapter 15 draw one set of patterns: today the patterns live in three build scripts
needs.N-13: Small multiples past four groups (DR-234) draw the other groups faint behind each panel; no token names that role

rules_with_the_palettes: Sequential: five Verdigris steps per ground, light to strong on Newsprint and dark to light on Charcoal, so the most always reads strongest. Print the value on or beside every step 1 to 3 fill.
Diverging: pair B only, Prussian for one side and Verdigris for the other, with a boxed arrow or a printed sign in every cell. Say in the key which side is which. Never red with blue.

Categorical: at most four groups, in the order Charcoal (Newsprint on Charcoal), Prussian, Verdigris, Stone. The Stone group always carries the hatch; every group carries a direct label and, on a line, its end marker. Never for parties.
Past four groups: small multiples with the other groups as ghosts, or one group in ink and every other in the context gray, every group labeled (DR-234).
Magnitude: gray Stone steps with no direction; the figure prints in every tile.
Grade line code: the line's width sets its pattern; no coded line drops under 2 px; a run under 28 widths prints its grade in words.
Red: one working red per view (Rule 05.3). A chart's red point yields to the subject ink when an error or an ask is in the view, and keeps its label and place.
